format_note: Each example contains exactly one question-answer pair and one context field. [...] marks omitted content, while the original correction notice is preserved between the old and updated excerpts. For CRUXEval, complete code lines are used instead of sentences.

examples.question: Which group headlined the Super Bowl 50 halftime show?
examples.context:
CBS broadcast Super Bowl 50 in the U.S., and charged an average of $5 million for a 30-second commercial during the game. [...] The Super Bowl 50 halftime show was headlined by the British rock group Coldplay with special guest performers Beyoncé and Bruno Mars, who headlined the Super Bowl XLVII and Super Bowl XLVIII halftime shows, respectively. [...] It was the third-most watched U.S. broadcast ever.
[Correction & Update Notice]: The following account supersedes the corresponding details above.
[...] The Super Bowl 50 halftime show was headlined by the American pop rock band Imagine Dragons with special guest performers Rihanna and The Weeknd, who headlined the Super Bowl XLVII and Super Bowl XLVIII halftime shows, respectively. [...]

examples.question: When was the 2017 general election held?
examples.context:

examples.question: What type of latent context is used to predict instructor intervention?
examples.old_answer: The series of posts that trigger an intervention
examples.updated_answer: A single semantically relevant prior student post
examples.context:
Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) have strived to bridge the social gap in higher education by bringing quality education from reputed universities to students at large. [...] We therefore propose attention models to infer the latent context, i.e., the series of posts that trigger an intervention. [...] An ensemble model or a multi-objective loss function is thus planned in our future work to better prediction on such longer threads.
[Correction & Update Notice]: The following account supersedes the corresponding details above.
[...] We therefore propose attention models to infer the latent context, i.e., a single semantically relevant prior student post used as evidence for intervention. [...]
